details:
* SECURITY UPDATE: daemon module-root chdir escape under `use chroot = no`
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-53784.patch: add safe_open_no_attacker_symlinks()
       to util.c and route change_dir()'s daemon module-root chdir through it, so
       a planted parent-component symlink no longer moves the daemon's CWD
       outside the module; a symlink is followed only when owned by uid 0 or our
       euid
     - CVE-2026-53784
   * SECURITY UPDATE: arbitrary file read via symlinked operator input paths
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-53802.patch: open --filter merge files (including
       per-directory merges and -C .cvsignore), --files-from/--include-from/
       --exclude-from (exclude.c) and the --password-file / daemon secrets file
       (authenticate.c) through the same ownership-checked walk, so a planted
       symlink cannot feed an arbitrary file to the filter parser or the
       authentication response
     - CVE-2026-53802
   * SECURITY UPDATE: arbitrary file write via symlinked operator output paths
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-53803.patch: open --log-file (log.c), the
       --write-batch/--read-batch files (batch.c and main.c) and the daemon motd,
       lock and --config paths (clientserver.c, connection.c, params.c) through
       the same ownership-checked walk, so a planted symlink cannot redirect a
       privileged write, and require --read-batch to name a regular file or a FIFO
     - CVE-2026-53803
   * NOTE: the ownership-checked path walk opens each intermediate directory
     for reading, where plain path resolution needed only search permission,
     so an operator path under a search-only (e.g. 0711) ancestor that the
     caller cannot read is now refused: --log-file falls back to syslog with
     a warning and --exclude-from fails. This matches upstream behaviour.
